findings.claim: Lemma C's sign-indefinite cross term tr(P^2 Q) re-opens the lambda_max/Lindelof branch of the recorded odd-moment no-go (transcript p.80, tx_081), which the proposal's obstruction-evasion section never addresses; the stated remainder form R <= eps*tr A^2 + C(eps)*(trace-asymmetry) does not cover it in the intermediate-depth regime.
findings.argument: tx_081 states the no-go in two parts: (a) an LP certificate p(mu)=c1 mu+c2 mu^2+c3 mu^3 <= 1 on (0,inf) needs c3<=0 and is then dominated by its quadratic part; (b) 'the third moment would help only together with an a-priori bound lambda_max(R~)=O(1), i.e. a pointwise bound for Sum_{n<=X} Lambda(n) n^{-1/2-i tau} on windows of length 1/L' — Lindelof-strength. The proposal evades (a) legitimately (integer-multiplicity cubic via majorization is outside the eigenvalue-valid class; 7.5(g) proves cubic beats quadratic under RH). It never mentions (b). Audit of rank_trace_cubic: with c3<=0, expand tr A^3 = tr P^3 + 3tr(P^2Q) + 3tr(PQ^2) + tr Q^3. tr(PQ^2)>=0 (both PSD) enters with favorable sign c3<0. tr Q^3: I VERIFIED the proposal's odd-trace near-cancellation claim — for a pair block 2m(xx^T-yy^T) with u=x+iy the evaluation vector, ||x||^2-||y||^2 = Re(sum_k u_k^2), and the sub-critical Gabor-Poisson identity gives sum_k phihat(g-tau_k)^2 = l*(phi*phi)(0) EXACTLY for all complex g (the m>=1 aliasing samples of phi*phi at +-l vanish for lambda_w<=1), so the per-block trace asymmetry is O(m*l), depth-independent and sign-definite; hence tr B^3 ~ 3 mu^2 * asym with asym = +2ml*int(phi^2) > 0, and c3<=0 makes tr Q^3 favorable too. The residual danger is exactly tr(P^2 Q) = sum_blocks 2m(||Px||^2 - ||Py||^2): sign-indefinite (no Poisson rigidity — it equals Re sum_{j,j'} m_j m_{j'} <v_j,v_{j'}> l^2 Phi(gamma_j - g)Phi(gamma_{j'} - g), position-dependent complex phases), controllable adversarially by micro-shifting the off-line ordinate by ~pi/(lambda l) to flip the phase of Phi at complex argument. Homogeneity check of the claimed pricing: per deep block |tr(P^2 B)| ~ X^y * l^a (a>=1 from local overlaps, larger with admissible clustering N(t+1)-N(t) ~ log t giving lambda_max(P) ~ l), the block's tr A^2 contribution is ~X^{2y}, and its asymmetry is O(ml). eps*tr A^2 covers only blocks with X^y >= l^a/eps; C(eps)*asym covers only O(l) per block. The intermediate regime X^y ~ polylog with K ~ N/polylog blocks (t2 budget K*X^{2y} <= eta*N respected, remaining traces matched within the o(main) tolerances by adjusting the standard extremal background) yields total unpriced junk ~ N * l^{power} >> the certified gain delta*N. So the Lean-hook statement of rank_trace_cubic with that remainder form is very likely false against the abstract configuration class, and any repair that bounds tr(P^2 Q) for the true zeta multiset appears to need ||P||_op-type control, i.e. the short-window P_X bounds of Remark 7.1(ii) — the known-hard sub-Lindelof threshold. The cited proof-of-concept 7.5(g) is Q-EMPTY (RH-conditional), so it evidences nothing about this term. The proposal's own mitigation (numerics (b) Monte Carlo) measures typical configurations, but validity must hold configuration-by-configuration; the G1-G4 history shows exactly this typical-vs-adversarial gap being fatal. Not scored fatal only because: (i) my l-power bookkeeping in the intermediate regime is a sketch and the campaign has previously produced surprising Poisson rigidities (as with the trace asymmetry) that could yet tame Re(u^T P^2 u); (ii) the proposal gates M3/M4 behind M1+MC and its failure modes name this risk. But the burden is on the proposal: as designed, the certificate arm collides with the recorded no-go's unaddressed branch rather than evading it.

findings.claim: The headline 'mixed-window corner' novelty rests on the paper's crude equal-window accounting (k*lambda<2 => lambda<2/3 at k=3) and is contradicted by the campaign's own sharper record: tx_081 states the odd-moment Fourier support reaches (k-1)*lambda, so k=3 is 'admissible on the whole useful range' lambda<1 with EQUAL windows — the proposal never reconciles the two, and its information-region claim is not new either way.
findings.argument: Shell geometry: the triple-trace functional only probes the sum-zero shell xi1+xi2+xi3=0. For equal windows |xi_i|<=lambda, the maximum of |xi1|+|xi2|+|xi1+xi2| on the shell is 2*lambda (one coordinate must balance the other two, and |xi3|<=lambda caps the balancing), so equal windows at lambda=0.98 already access a region with total support 1.96<2 — a STRICT SUPERSET of the mixed (0.98,0.5,0.5) region, which additionally constrains |xi2|<=0.5. Hence 'one factor at pair-bandwidth ~1, a corner the equal-window analysis never touched' is false at the level of accessible support: mixed windows are a restriction, not an extension, of the equal-window region at lambda_max. What is genuinely at issue is the PROOF range: the proposal's absolute-value MV accounting needs sigma=lambda_a+lambda_b+lambda_c<2 because the far-off-diagonal (|log(n1 n2/n3)| >~ 1, suppressed only by the ~1/(y-z) Dirichlet-kernel tails of the sharp k<d grid cutoff, no rapid decay) carries ell^1 mass ~ sqrt(X_a X_b)*sqrt(X_c) = T^{sigma/2}; tx_081's lambda<1 claim for equal windows would need genuine cancellation there (or relies on its admittedly from-memory RS recall). So either (i) tx_081 is right, and the mixed-window innovation is vacuous — equal windows at lambda->1 already deliver the third trace, which is precisely the situation in which tx_081 then derived the odd-moment no-go — or (ii) the proposal's sigma<2 is the honest boundary, in which case its 'Rudnick-Sarnak boundary re-derived' framing should be presented as the absolute-value-MV boundary and the internal contradiction with the campaign record must be resolved explicitly. The surviving novelty is real but much narrower than claimed: mixed windows enlarge the achievable KERNEL CONE (products Phi_a x Phi_b x Phi_c with three distinct windows, useful for LP rows) within a support region that is not new.

findings.claim: M1's LP overstates the provable data class: it pins every triple row A3(j1,j2) within a uniform tolerance tau3, but T1 delivers only smooth product-kernel functionals Phi_a x Phi_b x Phi_c on the shell, each with its own o(1) error; the go/no-go readout p0^(3)-p0^(2)>0.02 is therefore biased toward 'go', and the M4 certificate cannot consume the rows as priced.
findings.argument: T1 (or RS-type input) yields, per window triple, ONE number: sum_{j1,j2} Phihat_a(j1)Phihat_b(j2)Phihat_c(j1+j2)-weighted combinations of the A3 observables, with an error at the theorem's o(main) scale. Recovering pointwise rows A3(j1,j2)=0 +- tau3 at all ~N^2/2 simplex points requires inverting a tensor-product-cone decomposition (delta-like kernels are not C^3-taper products; the decomposition's ell^1 coefficient mass multiplies the per-instance tolerances), so the certified tolerance at a single grid point degrades by the conditioning of that decomposition — potentially by large factors at N=64-128. An LP whose adversary must match all pointwise rows within a uniform small tau3 is strictly more constrained than one facing only the achievable cone, so p0^(3) computed as designed is an upper bound on the true worth of the upgrade, and the M1 decision gate can pass while the honest (achievable-cone) value collapses toward p0^(2). Likewise the LP dual weights may correspond to a non-achievable kernel, in which case 'the candidate optimal certificate whose validity Lemma C must prove' is not fed by T1 at all. Repair is clean and should be mandatory: parameterize LP rows by the achievable product-kernel cone (mixed windows legitimately enrich it — see finding 2) with propagated tolerances, and re-anchor the 0.02 gate on that LP.

findings.claim: The 'first unconditional correlation theorem for zeta zeros beyond order 2' headline (novelty 1, milestone M2) rests on an unverified negative claim about Rudnick-Sarnak 1996 that the campaign's own record contradicts: tx_081 recalls RS 'prove the n-level correlations are GUE for Sum|xi_j|<2 and state explicitly that RH is not assumed' for zeta.
findings.argument: If RS 1996 (Duke 81) is unconditional for zeta on the full class of test functions with hat-support in Sum|xi_j|<2 — as the tx_081 agent explicitly recalls, and as is consistent with BGSTB24 having targeted only the Montgomery-F(alpha)-specific weighted form at the pair level — then T1's content reduces to: RS's theorem + the (exact, easy) Gabor-Poisson repackaging into mixed Gram traces + explicit error terms, and both novelty claim (1) ('exists in print only under RH') and M2's standalone-headline payoff are wrong. The proposal flags this for verification but nonetheless builds its milestone-payoff structure ('standalone headline theorem... independent of the certificate program's fate') and its BGSTB-analogy framing on the unverified branch. Note the two-sided effect: if RS is unconditional the route's FEASIBILITY improves (the analytic input may be quotable rather than provable-from-scratch, de-risking M2) while the payoff collapses to a technical variant; if RS is conditional, M2 stands but the tx_081-based equal-window claim in finding 2 weakens. Either resolution materially changes the proposal's expected value, and it must be resolved (against the original paper, not memory) before any M2 spend.

findings.claim: The cited proof-of-concept (Section 7.5(g), f(x)=-x^2/9+x^3/18, N_d>=0.85082 under RH) uses the opposite certificate direction from Lemma C: convex f with c3=+1/18>0 consumed via Schur-Horn (sum f(m_j) <= tr f(A)), whereas the proposal's validity polynomial forces c3<=0 and the concave Schur-Jensen direction; 'cubic accounting survives interactions' in the convex direction is automatic majorization and is not evidence about Lemma C's actual content.
findings.argument: psi(m)=c1 m+c2 m^2+c3 m^3+c4*1_{m=1} <= 1 on all integers m>=1 forces c3<=0 (else psi->+inf), and the certificate consumes sum psi(m_j) >= trace-combo - penalties, i.e. the concave/Schur-Jensen direction (which also forces c2<=0 for concavity on [0,inf)). 7.5(g)'s f has positive cubic coefficient and is consumed in the convex/Schur-Horn direction (upper-bounding sum f(m_j) by the trace to penalize high multiplicities). For a single PSD matrix in Gram coordinates both directions are the same diagonal-vs-eigenvalue majorization fact, so the P-only 'survival of interactions' is trivial in both; everything hard in Lemma C is the Q-mixed terms (finding 1), about which 7.5(g) — being Q-empty — says nothing. The citation should be corrected from 'proof-of-concept that cubic accounting survives interactions' to 'proof that a third trace has nonzero certificate value in the Q-free case'; as written it overstates the evidential support for the route's core lemma.

findings.claim: T1's core MV mechanics are sound (verified), but the proposal's 'ratio-type frequencies are handled identically' glosses the one place its own hardest risk lives, and the same-prime-power and near-diagonal bookkeeping deserve one caveat each.
findings.argument: Verified in the proposal's favor: (i) the spacing-weighted MV norms are computed correctly — with coefficients (Lambda*Lambda)(m)/sqrt(m) and delta_m >= 1/(2m), |a_m|^2/delta_m = 2(Lambda*Lambda)(m)^2, and sum_{m<=Y}(Lambda*Lambda)(m)^2 ~ c Y log^3 Y (partial summation over sum_p (log p)^2/p), giving the claimed l^2 T^{sigma/2} = o(T l^3) iff sigma<2; (ii) the near-diagonal band |log(m/n3)|<=1/T is empty since the resonance forces m ~ n3 <= X_c <= T so |m-n3| <= m/T < 1; (iii) exact relations n1 n2 = n3 among prime powers force a common prime, and sum_p (log p)^3 sum_{a,b} p^{-a-b} converges — subleading as claimed; (iv) the three-fold Poisson resummation to the zero side is exact at sub-critical sampling for all lambda_w <= 1 (the aliasing samples of phi*phi at the closed endpoint +-l vanish by continuity). The caveat: the far-off-diagonal is suppressed only by first-order Dirichlet-kernel decay from the sharp k<d grid cutoff (no smooth T-taper is present in the trace), which is exactly why sigma<2 is the absolute-value boundary (finding 2) and why any endpoint improvement or the fallback erosion to sigma<3/2 would shrink both the accessible simplex and the LP value — consistent with, but sharper than, the proposal's own flagged risk.

run1_killer.repairs: 1) RECONCILE WITH THE CAMPAIGN RECORD (blocks everything else): resolve the tx_081 vs sigma<2 discrepancy on the equal-window k=3 range, and resolve the unconditional status of Rudnick-Sarnak 1996 (and Hejhal 1994) against the originals before any M2 spend. If RS is unconditional for zeta, recast M2 as 'Gram-trace packaging with explicit errors, mixed-window kernel cone' (quotable input, lower risk, lower payoff) and delete 'first unconditional triple correlation' from the payoff ledger. 2) NAME THE LAMBDA_MAX LOCK AS AN OBSTRUCTION: add the second branch of the tx_081 odd-moment no-go ('third moment helps only with lambda_max = O(1)') to the obstruction-evasion table with a real evasion — concretely, either exhibit a Poisson/functional-equation rigidity for Re(u^T P^2 u) analogous to the (verified) trace-asymmetry rigidity, or restate rank_trace_cubic with a remainder that explicitly carries the tr(P^2 Q) overlap term and show the LP dual still clears the gate with that term priced adversarially. 3) FIX THE M1 LP DATA CLASS: rows must span only the achievable product-kernel cone Phi_a x Phi_b x Phi_c (this is where mixed windows genuinely earn their keep) with tolerances propagated from the theorem's error terms; re-anchor the 0.02 decision gate there. Report both p0^(3)-pointwise (upper bound on the upgrade's worth) and p0^(3)-achievable (honest value). 4) HARDEN NUMERICS (B) FROM TYPICAL TO ADVERSARIAL: add the specific stress family from finding 1 — intermediate-depth pairs (X^y ~ polylog, K ~ N/polylog of them) with ordinates micro-shifted by ~pi/(lambda l) to phase-tune Phi at complex argument, on top of an admissible log-density cluster — and require the measured worst-case interaction penalty as an LP row before any M3 proof attempt. 5) FIX THE 7.5(g) CITATION (direction mismatch) and demote the M4 stretch goal (certified value above 0.6818287) to conditional-on-Lemma-C. 6) KEEP AND FOREGROUND THE ROBUST DELIVERABLES: the pair-only LP dual at N=128 (the 0.6725->0.6818 gap certificate, verifiable in the existing Lean Stability harness) and the M5 formal multilinear ceiling are valuable regardless of Lemma C's fate and should be promoted from by-products to primary milestones.
literature_flags: Rudnick-Sarnak 1996 (Duke Math. J. 81, 'Zeros of principal L-functions and random matrix theory'): does the n-level correlation theorem for zeta hold UNCONDITIONALLY (complex ordinates, test functions with hat-support in Sum|xi|<2)? tx_081 recalls 'state explicitly that RH is not assumed' (from memory, not fetched); the proposal's novelty claim (1) and M2 headline require the opposite. Decisive either way — must be checked against the original.
Hejhal 1994 (triple correlation of zeta zeros): proposal assumes RH-conditional; verify, including whether any remark de-conditionalizes for zeta.

Diaconis-Shahshahani exactness: verify the precise condition under which E[Tr U^{j1} Tr U^{j2} Tr U^{-(j1+j2)}] = 0 for CUE(N) — the standard statement requires sum of weighted degrees <= N on each side; confirm behavior AT the boundary j1+j2=N, which the LP's free-edge design assumes matches the pair-row edge treatment.

Paper Section 7.5(e): the proposal quotes the equal-window range as k*lambda<2 (=> lambda<2/3 at k=3), while transcript tx_081 gives (k-1)*lambda<2 (=> lambda<1) for odd k — verify which the paper actually asserts and whether either is proved anywhere with errors.

Paper Section 7.5(g): confirm f(x) = -x^2/9 + x^3/18, window cos(8s/5), N_d >= 0.85082, RH-conditional with Q empty, and the exact sense of the Schur-Horn majorization step (convex direction), which the proposal cites as evidence for the opposite-direction concave inequality.
BGSTB24 = arXiv:2306.04799 (unconditional Montgomery pair theorem, complex ordinates) — confirmed consistent with results/literature.md; the proposal's use is accurate at the pair level.

GLSS arXiv:2503.15449 and arXiv:2507.06823 as pair-only (AH analysis) — consistent with literature.md; the M6 claim that AH-structured laws violate triple rows is speculative in both directions and is correctly gated on the M1 LP.

findings.claim: T1's headline novelty ('first unconditional triple correlation for zeta, strictly stronger than anything in print') is overstated: it is a careful write-up of technology the parent artifact itself asserts as available, and its status as a 'first' hinges entirely on an unverified reading of Rudnick-Sarnak 1996.
findings.argument: Three independent deflations. (a) The Zeta23 paper itself asserts (Section 7.5(e), full-map.md line 92) that 'the diagonal method evaluates tr G-hat^k exactly in the Rudnick-Sarnak range k*lambda < 2' -- i.e., the artifact's authors regard the equal-window unconditional case as known technology, merely never written with error terms. A theorem the parent paper asserts in a remark is not 'strictly stronger than anything in print' in the sense the proposal's payoff section implies; it is the write-up of an assertion. (b) The artifact reads Hejhal 1994 / Rudnick-Sarnak 1996 as RH-conditional (full-map.md line 95: 'Under RH the third trace/triple correlation is a theorem [Hej94, RS96] for lambda<1'), which supports the proposal, BUT Rudnick-Sarnak's Duke 1996 paper is widely recalled to contain a remark that for zeta their n-level results hold unconditionally with complex ordinates (their test functions are Paley-Wiener, entire of exponential type -- exactly what complex-ordinate de-conditionalization needs). If that remark exists and is sound, T1 reduces to: explicit error terms + trace-formalism packaging of a 30-year-old theorem. The proposal flags this itself, but then still books M2 as 'standalone headline theorem (first unconditional triple correlation)' -- the milestone payoff is priced on the optimistic branch of an unresolved literature question. (c) The 'mixed windows' framing is novelty relative to the Zeta23 paper's tr G^k equal-window presentation, not relative to the literature: Rudnick-Sarnak's theorem is stated for general test functions with Fourier support in the simplex sum|xi_i| < 2, which already contains every kernel the mixed-window construction can produce. My own computation (finding 2) confirms the union of mixed-window boxes over sigma < 2 is exactly the open RS simplex -- i.e., mixed windows recover, via crude MV, precisely the data class RS already defined. Correct classification: T1 = new combination / careful de-conditionalized write-up (BGSTB24 precedent shows such write-ups are genuinely publishable and nontrivial -- BGSTB was new in 2023 despite RS's remark), not a new object. The BGSTB precedent is the strongest argument that T1 has real content; the proposal should be reframed around it.

findings.claim: The support bookkeeping conflates the window-sum sigma = lambda_a+lambda_b+lambda_c with the kernel's simplex support, and the flagship mixed-window example is numerically wrong: (0.98, 0.5, 0.5) does NOT put any factor at pair-bandwidth ~1; it reaches only |xi| <= 0.74.
findings.argument: Write the kernel Phi_a(g1-g2)Phi_b(g2-g3)Phi_c(g3-g1) in Fourier form with u_w in supp(phi_w^2) = [-lambda_w/2, lambda_w/2] in Montgomery alpha-units (this normalization is fixed by the pair case: tr G^2 has kernel Phi^2 with support [-lambda, lambda], matching 'bandwidth one = |alpha| <= 1'). The frequency hitting zero-ordinate g1 is xi_1 = u_a - u_c, similarly xi_2 = u_b - u_a, xi_3 = u_c - u_b; so |xi_1| <= (lambda_a + lambda_c)/2. For (0.98, 0.5, 0.5): max|xi_1| = 0.74, max|xi_2| = 0.74, max|xi_3| = 0.5 -- no direction near 1. Reaching one direction at ~1 requires lambda_a + lambda_c ~ 2, which under sigma < 2 forces lambda_b ~ 0, i.e. triples like (0.99, 0.01, 0.99) where the middle window sees primes only up to T^{0.01} -- a near-degenerate factor. Two consequences. (i) The advertised corner 'one factor at full pair bandwidth with two substantive companions' does not exist; the accessible corner has one nearly-arithmetic-free window. (ii) The correct general statement, which I verified, is: for a target frequency point (xi_1,xi_2,xi_3) on the hyperplane, the minimal window sum needed is sigma_min = sum|xi_i| (solve u_a - u_c = xi_1 etc., center at the median: min_c 2*sum|u_i - c| = 2*(max u - min u) = sum|xi_i|). Hence the union of mixed-window boxes over sigma < 2 is EXACTLY the open RS simplex {sum|xi_i| < 2} -- the thesis survives in corrected form, and this also reconciles the artifact's two seemingly inconsistent statements (7.5(e): unconditional crude MV needs 3*lambda < 2 per equal-window triple; 7.5(g): RS/Hejhal triple correlation available for lambda < 1, since equal-window kernel support is 2*lambda). REPAIR: restate the mechanism with sigma_min = sum|xi_i|, fix the example, and have the M1 LP price the actual accessible box family (products of three intervals in u-space), not the abstract simplex -- the binding rows may sit at points requiring a near-trivial window, which changes what T1 must deliver.

findings.claim: Lemma C (rank_trace_cubic) is substantially harder than the proposal's 'single genuinely new piece of linear algebra' framing admits: the mixed triple trace is not an odd moment of any single Hermitian matrix, the formalized Schur-Jensen pillar does not cover it, and the 7.5(g) proof-of-concept depends on positive semidefiniteness that fails exactly when Q is nonempty.
findings.argument: Four gaps. (i) Non-Hermitian product: tr(G_a G_b G_c) with three distinct Hermitian G's satisfies conj(tr(G_aG_bG_c)) = tr(G_aG_cG_b) != tr(G_aG_bG_c) in general; only the symmetrized real part is canonically real. All majorization/Schur-Horn/von Neumann machinery in the repo is single-matrix; there is no formalized (or paper-level) calculus for signed products of three non-commuting indefinite compressions. 7.5(g) (full-map.md line 95) is single-window tr H^3 with H = M^{1/2} Gamma M^{1/2} >= 0 under RH. (ii) The PSD hypothesis is load-bearing twice: the Lean lemma sum_gc_diag_le_sum_gc_eigenvalues (RankTraceMult.lean:119) requires M.PosSemidef, and 7.5(g)'s convex-majorization step uses f(x) = x^3/18 - x^2/9 which is convex only for x >= 2/3; with Q nonempty the spectrum contains large NEGATIVE eigenvalues (hyperbolic blocks at depth y have eigenvalues ~ +-X^{lambda y}) where f is concave -- the majorization inequality direction breaks and must be replaced by exactly the interaction-remainder accounting R that the proposal defers. (iii) The odd-trace near-cancellation is real but subtler than stated: for an isolated block with eigenvalues s/2 +- m (s = block trace asymmetry, m ~ ||u||*||v||), tr B^3 = 2s'^3 + 6s'm^2-type, i.e. it grows like (asymmetry)*X^{2*lambda*y}, and the per-block asymmetry s ~ l*Phi_w(i(2beta-1)) is itself of size X^{lambda y} -- NOT O(1). What saves validity is a sign observation the proposal never makes explicit: s has deterministic positive sign because Phi_w(iy) = integral of phi_w^2 * e^{yu} du > 0, so with c3 <= 0 isolated deep blocks strictly DECREASE the certificate's left side (validity-safe, value-costly). The un-saved part is precisely the cross terms tr(P^2Q), tr(PQ^2) and inter-block products, where relative phases oscillate and no sign is forced -- the same interaction mechanism that killed per-pair quadratic pricing at order 2 (G1-G4). The Monte Carlo gate (numerics B) is the right mitigation and the proposal deserves credit for measuring before proving, but the Lean hook's claim that the skeleton 'already covers cubic g' is half-false: sum_eigenvalues_comm is indeed general (arbitrary g with g(0)=0, verified at RankTraceMult.lean:189), but the Schur-Jensen lemma is formalized ONLY for the specific quadratic-type function gc and PSD matrices -- extending it is real new formal and mathematical work. M3 is the miracle step; I would price its success at ~0.3, well below the ambient optimism.

findings.claim: The 'free by-product' -- pair-only LP dual closing the 0.6725 -> 0.6818 gap -- conflates LP value-optimality with certificate validity; nothing in the existing machinery can validate an arbitrary dual weight r.
findings.argument: Theorem D is proved optimal within 'block structure + two traces + primes up to T' via [CCLM17 Cor 14] (full-map.md line 75: 'no window does better'), so any certificate exceeding 0.6725 within bandwidth one necessarily uses a functional format for which NO analytic realization currently exists -- the map's transcript hook says exactly this ('richer functionals of bandwidth-one data'). The LP dual at N=128 produces candidate weights (c0, r) that are optimal against the FEASIBLE SET of the LP, but certificate validity is the zero-side inequality 'c0 + sum_j S(j/N) r(j/N) <= p for every admissible configuration', which for the paper's certificates is supplied by Lemma 3.2 + window structure, not by the LP. The Lean Stability/RowCert harness verifies VALUES against a fixed law (lean:ceiling section: 'no formalized matching certificate ... that bridge is a paper-level remark'), not validity for zeta. So the by-product is: candidate weights plus a two-sided numerical gap -- genuinely useful, but 'closing the gap' requires a new validity lemma of unknown difficulty. The milestone text should say so.

findings.claim: M4's simple-zero payoff (delta_s > 0, stretch delta_s > 0.0094) is the least-supported number in the ladder, and the LP's binding triple rows will plausibly concentrate at the simplex edge where T1 degrades -- so realizable payoff is likely systematically below p0^(3).
findings.argument: (i) The only existence proof that a third trace buys anything (7.5(g), +0.0146) is for the DISTINCT count N_d, under RH, with Q empty; the transcript's Theorem U (full-map.md line 166) shows the odd moment adds nothing to the [0,infinity)-count/Christoffel route absent Lindelof-strength lambda_max control. The proposal's evasion (integrality atoms + the 1_{m=1} term + mixed windows, outside Theorem U's continuous-spectrum LP-dual) is legitimate but means the ENTIRE simple-count payoff rests on the M1 computation; the 'predicted range 0.69-0.73' has no calculation behind it. (ii) Structural worry not listed in the failure modes: at order 2 the 256-law's whole advantage was the FREE EDGE row j = N (edge atom mass 0.826; lean:ceiling: 'the LP's entire advantage lives in the free row j = N'). By the same mechanism, the order-3 LP's binding constraints will likely sit near the simplex boundary j1 + j2 = N, exactly where T1's error terms blow up (endpoint sigma -> 2, loglog/log losses) and where realizing the kernel requires a near-degenerate window (finding 2). REPAIR: run M1 additionally with triple rows restricted to j1 + j2 <= (1-eps)N for eps in {0.02, 0.05, 0.1} and report p0^(3)(eps); if the gain evaporates for small edge retreats, the analytic program is moot and this is discovered for the price of a few LP solves.

findings.claim: M6's Alternative-Hypothesis refutation may have prior art in the point-process literature; the claim 'first test of AH against 3-level data' needs a literature check before being advertised.
findings.argument: GLSS arXiv:2507.06823 is pair-only (consistent with the proposal), but there exist constructions of full AH-compatible POINT PROCESSES (Tao's 'alternative hypothesis' construction, and related work by Lagarias-Rodgers on differences), and it is not known to this referee whether any of them is proved consistent with restricted-range 3-level correlations. Two branches: if such a process exists matching triple data on the simplex, M6's refutation hope is dead (and the M1 LP will find the corresponding law -- cheap discovery, good design); if not, the M1 LP result would be genuinely new. Either way the proposal's phrasing 'potential first refutation of AH from provable-range data' is acceptable as exploratory, but the write-up must check the AH point-process literature first. Related credit: the observation that AH's rigid half-integer spacings should generate in-band triple resonances j1+j2=j3 is plausible and concrete.

findings.claim: Verified-correct core claims (reported for the record, since several load-bearing recalled facts survive scrutiny): the Diaconis-Shahshahani exactness claim, the composite-frequency MV arithmetic, and the artifact-constant citations are all accurate.
findings.argument: (i) DS exactness: E[p_mu(U) conj(p_nu(U))] = delta_{mu,nu} z_mu for partitions with |mu|, |nu| <= N (Diaconis-Shahshahani 1994, refined Diaconis-Evans 2001); applying it to mu = (j1, j2), nu = (j1+j2), both of size j1+j2 <= N, gives E[Tr U^{j1} Tr U^{j2} conj(Tr U^{j1+j2})] = 0 exactly, as claimed. Important subtlety the proposal handles correctly: this does NOT mean the connected 3-level CLUSTER function has vanishing Fourier transform on the simplex (the sine-kernel T_3 transform is nonzero there); it means the full trace moment -- cluster integral PLUS coincidence/diagonal terms -- vanishes, which is exactly T1's form ('triple sum equals its pairing/diagonal value'). The proposed Monte Carlo sanity check of t3 will confirm this translation. (ii) MV arithmetic: sum_{m<=Y} (Lambda*Lambda)(m)^2 ~ c*Y*log^3(Y) (dominant contribution from m = pq squarefree: 4*sum_p log^2 p * (Y/p) log(Y/p) ~ c Y l^3), and the bilinear geometric-mean form of MV is obtainable from the Hermitian union-family inequality by the standard t-scaling optimization, giving off-diagonal << (Y l^3)^{1/2} (X_c l)^{1/2} = l^2 T^{sigma/2} = o(T l^3) iff sigma < 2 -- the sketch's arithmetic is right, and ratio frequencies work at the same order because the 1/(n1 n2) coefficient weights compensate the Farey spacings. (iii) Artifact constants check out: psi(m) = m/2 + (2m^2 - m^3)/18 + (4/9)1_{m=1}, window cos(8s/5), N_d >= 0.85082 vs pair-only 0.83625, CGdL20 0.8477 distinct / 0.6792 simple, 5/6 = Theorem C, ceiling 0.6818287, gap 0.0093-0.0094, HL*(4) = 13/18. The cited Lean artifacts exist as claimed (spacing_four, two_point, sum_eigenvalues_comm), with the one misdescription noted in finding 3. This is an unusually well-grounded proposal at the level of constants and repo facts.

run1_referee.repairs: Four repairs, none fatal. (1) Reframe T1's novelty on the BGSTB precedent: 'de-conditionalized, fully-error-termed n=3 correlation in trace form' rather than 'first unconditional triple correlation', with the RS96 verification (does their unconditional complex-ordinate remark exist, and does it cover the needed uniformity/test class?) done in month 0 -- it changes only the marketing of M2, not its use by the certificate. (2) Fix the support bookkeeping: replace the false example (0.98, 0.5, 0.5) with the correct statement sigma_min = sum|xi_i| (union of mixed-window boxes = full open RS simplex; one direction at bandwidth ~1 forces one near-trivial window), and make the M1 LP price the actual accessible kernel family (u-space box products) with an edge-retreat study p0^(3)(eps) for triple rows restricted to j1+j2 <= (1-eps)N -- this measures both the mixed-window corner's real worth and the endpoint-degradation exposure before any analytic spend. (3) Add an explicit fallback certificate architecture for M3: single-window cubic tr(G_b^3) at lambda_b < 2/3 (Hermitian, avoids the non-Hermitian mixed-product calculus entirely) consumed JOINTLY with lambda ~ 1 pair data as a two-compression certificate -- strictly easier linear algebra, priceable by the same LP as a separate row block; keep the mixed version as the stretch. Budget real work for generalizing the Schur-Jensen lemma (currently gc-specific and PosSemidef-only) to cubic g on indefinite spectra. (4) Downgrade the pair-only-dual by-product to 'candidate weights + two-sided gap' and add the required new validity lemma to the M4 task list; check the AH point-process literature (Tao's construction, Lagarias-Rodgers) before advertising M6. With these repairs the program is well-ordered: M1 is a genuinely informative computation the artifact itself calls 'the most informative next computation', T1/M2 is publishable regardless of the certificate's fate, and the two decision gates (LP delta > 0.02; Monte Carlo interaction measurement) are placed before the expensive steps.
literature_flags: Rudnick-Sarnak 1996 (Duke Math. J. 81): verify whether their n-level correlation theorem for zeta is stated/provable unconditionally with complex ordinates (their remark on not assuming RH), and whether their test-function class and uniformity cover T1's mixed-window kernels -- DECISIVE for M2's 'first unconditional triple correlation' claim; the Zeta23 artifact reads them as RH-conditional (full-map.md line 95) but this is the artifact's recall, not a verified fact.
Hejhal 1994 (IMRN, triple correlation of zeta zeros): confirm RH-conditionality and the exact support range of his test class.

Diaconis-Shahshahani 1994 (J. Appl. Probab. 31A) and Diaconis-Evans 2001 (Trans. AMS 353): confirm the exact moment-matching range |mu|, |nu| <= N used for the claim E[Tr U^{j1} Tr U^{j2} conj(Tr U^{j1+j2})] = 0 for j1+j2 <= N (my derivation supports it, but the LP rows' t3 = 0 values inherit any error here; the proposed CUE Monte Carlo sanity check should be mandatory, not optional).

BGSTB arXiv:2306.04799: confirmed present in literature.md as the unconditional pair-correlation theorem; T1's complex-ordinate/tail treatment should be checked against their actual handling of off-line zeros (the X^{sigma/2} tail factor at sigma near 2 is the analogue of their hardest term).

GLSS arXiv:2503.15449 and arXiv:2507.06823: confirmed pair-only in literature.md; but ALSO check Tao's Alternative-Hypothesis point-process construction (blog/notes, ~2019) and Lagarias-Rodgers for whether an AH-consistent process matching restricted 3-level correlations is already known -- decisive for M6's 'first refutation of AH' ambition.
Chirre-Goncalves-de Laat [CGdL20]: verify the 0.6792 (simple, under RH with F >= 0 for |alpha| > 1) and 0.8477 (distinct) figures cited from the map.

Zeta23 paper Section 7.5(e)/(g): the proposal's account (equal-window tr G^k asserted by 'the diagonal method' without error terms; 0.85082 via psi(m) = m/2 + (2m^2-m^3)/18 + (4/9)1_{m=1}, window cos(8s/5), input N^s >= (19/27)N from [BHB13]) matches full-map.md lines 41, 92, 95 exactly -- verified against the map, but the map is itself a condensation; spot-check the paper pages in sources-extracted/ before quoting in print.

Internal artifact tension worth resolving in print: 7.5(e) claims unconditional third moment needs 3*lambda < 2 (crude MV) while 7.5(g) claims the RH-conditional third trace exists for lambda < 1 (kernel support 2*lambda < 2) -- the proposal's mixed-window construction is exactly what bridges these, and stating this reconciliation explicitly would strengthen the paper.

findings.claim: The central zero-side identity is mathematically wrong: tr(G_a G_b G_c) has CROSS-window kernels with Fourier supports min(lambda_i, lambda_j), not the claimed per-window kernels Phi_w with supports lambda_w. The headline 'mixed-window corner with one factor at pair-bandwidth ~1' does not exist in the proposed construction.
findings.argument: In tr(G_aG_bG_c) = Sum_{k1k2k3}(G_a)_{k1k2}(G_b)_{k2k3}(G_c)_{k3k1}, the shared grid index k2 pairs the right slot of G_a with the left slot of G_b. The k2-sum is Sum_{k2} conj(phihat_a(gbar1 - tau_k2)) phihat_b(g2 - tau_k2); Poisson over the grid of spacing 2pi/l gives l*(phi_a phi_b)^hat(g2 - gbar1) (exact since (lambda_a+lambda_b)l/2 < l). The u-integrand is the PRODUCT phi_a*phi_b, supported in the INTERSECTION of supports, so the kernel bandwidth is min(lambda_a, lambda_b). The proposal's formula 'l^3 Sum m1m2m3 Phi_a(g1-g2)Phi_b(g2-g3)Phi_c(g3-g1)' with Phi_w = (phi_w^2)^hat, and the support claim '{xi1+xi2+xi3=0, |xi_w| <= lambda_w}', are both false unless all windows are equal (the quoted Poisson identity is a same-window identity, but adjacent factors in the trace pair DIFFERENT windows). Consequence: the accessible triple-kernel supports are (s1,s2,s3) = (min(a,b), min(b,c), min(c,a)). Maximizing s1+s2+s3 subject to a+b+c < 2, all <= 1 (WLOG a<=b<=c, total = 2a+b) forces a=b=c: the total-support-2 boundary is attained ONLY at equal windows 2/3 — exactly the corner the parent paper already names (kLambda < 2, k=3). At the proposal's flagship point (0.98, 0.5, 0.5) the kernels have supports (0.5, 0.5, 0.5), total 1.5 — strictly LESS information than equal windows at 2/3, and no factor anywhere near pair-bandwidth 1. Getting s1 -> 1 would need lambda_a = lambda_b -> 1, forcing lambda_c < 0. So T1 as stated (connected-triple vanishing on the full sigma < 2 simplex via this construction) is wrongly derived, novelty claim (1) and the PairCeiling-evasion mechanism ('degree-3 rows carrying one bandwidth-1 direction') collapse, and this is consistent with the artifact's own scoping (tr G^k available for k*lambda < 2 — the paper's equal-window boundary is not an oversight but the true optimum of this construction). A repair exists — two-slot non-Hermitian G_w = W(phi_w^L e_{tau_k}, phi_w^R e_{tau_l}) with slot budget Sum_w(lambda_w^L + lambda_w^R)/2 < 2 reaches the full simplex s1+s2+s3 < 2 including (1-eps, 0.49, 0.49) — but it destroys Hermiticity, and the entire certificate side (Sylvester inertia, n_+, Schur-Jensen, rank_trace_cubic) requires Hermitian compressions. So the repaired T1 survives only as a standalone correlation theorem; the certificate arm is confined to the equal-window <= 2/3 box.

findings.claim: The proposal's own first formalizable statement, rank_trace_cubic, is FALSE as stated: explicit counterexamples with zero block trace-asymmetry violate it unboundedly for any c3 < 0. The interaction currency needed to repair it has no prime-side evaluation — this is the G1-G4 'free mass mover' failure one degree up, and at odd degree there is no positivity to fall back on.
findings.argument: Stated target: for P = Sum m_j v_j v_j^dagger, Q Hermitian = sum of blocks B_i with n_+(B_i) <= 1, any weights with psi(m) <= 1 (forcing c3 <= 0): Sum psi(m_j) + q(c)b >= c1 tr A + c2 tr A^2 + c3 tr A^3 - R, with R <= eps*tr A^2 + C(eps)*(block trace-asymmetries). Counterexample: P = 0; B_i = mu(e_i e_i^dagger - w w^dagger), i = 1..p, with orthonormal e_i and w orthogonal to all e_i. Each B_i has eigenvalues {+mu, -mu}, n_+(B_i) = 1, tr B_i = 0 (zero asymmetry). Q = mu*Sum e_ie_i^dagger - p*mu*ww^dagger has spectrum {+mu (x p), -p*mu}: tr A = 0, tr A^2 = (p + p^2)mu^2, tr A^3 = (p - p^3)mu^3 < 0. For any c3 < 0 the RHS contains |c3|(p^3-p)mu^3 while LHS = q(c)p is fixed and R <= eps(p+p^2)mu^2 + 0; letting mu -> infinity violates the inequality. If one objects that zeta-blocks have the outer-product form m(uw^dagger + wu^dagger) (under which shared-w blocks collapse to a single harmless hyperbolic pair), take two blocks with shared amplified direction u1 = u2 and misaligned damped directions (w2 perp w1, <w2,u1> = -t): tr(B1^2 B2) = ||w1||^2 * 2Re(<u1,u2><w2,u1>) * mu^3-scale = -2t*mu^3 — signed cross terms of size mu^3 with all block traces zero. Realizable-shaped: off-line zeros at nearby heights have substantially overlapping evaluation vectors (the transcript's cluster-visibility remark), and sign/alignment is adversary-tunable via positions. The abstract zero-side layer ('contains no arithmetic', arbitrary reflection-invariant multisets — the architecture the Lean formalization is built on) must admit these configurations, so the lemma needs either (i) a new hypothesis tying u_i to w_i geometrically — configuration-localization input that the invariant list cannot express and whose verification at zeta is blocked by the visibility/interference wall — or (ii) an interaction remainder containing signed cross-block cubic overlaps, which have NO prime-side evaluation: the prime side computes only the three traces, and at degree 3 the global trace does not one-sidedly bound individual pieces because odd-degree terms carry signs. This is the precise structural reason degree 2 works (||A||_F^2 is a sum of squares, so the global MV-bounded second moment automatically caps every block's X^{2y} mass, making n_+-only pricing valid) and degree 3 cannot: 'the zero-side second moment cannot be read termwise' becomes, at degree 3, 'the cubic cannot be read termwise AND has no positive global reading'. Generic Schatten-Holder gives |tr(ABC)| <= prod ||.||_{S3} <= prod ||.||_{S2} ~ (kappa N)^{3/2} = N^{3/2}, useless for o(N) accounting; any better split needs an operator-norm bound — the repo's named Lindelof lock. The proposal's evasion ('c3 <= 0 means mass escaping to large eigenvalues only hurts the adversary') addresses only the ON-LINE large-m escape (the LP-dual odd-moment no-go); the off-line signed-interaction escape is the actual killer and is untouched. M3 and hence M4's headline (beating 0.6818287, improving 5/6) are dead as designed.

findings.claim: M1 prices an unobtainable data class: triple rows on the full simplex j1+j2 <= N, when the certificate-compatible (Hermitian) construction only reaches the box j1, j2, j1+j2 <= (2/3)N — and the deleted rows are precisely the plausibly-binding ones (near-edge triples taxing the 256-law's edge atom). The decision gate can pass spuriously and the predicted range 0.69-0.73 is unfounded.
findings.argument: By finding 1, provable triple data for Hermitian compressions lives at kernel supports <= 2/3 per direction, i.e. LP rows A3(j1,j2) with j1, j2, j1+j2 <= (2/3)N — about 44% of the proposed row region, and crucially excluding all rows with j1+j2 in ((2/3)N, N). The 256-law's entire advantage lives in the free edge row j = N (atom mass ~0.826 per the Lean ceiling analysis); the triple rows that would most plausibly tax that structure are those coupling in-band frequencies to near-edge ones (j1 + j2 close to N, constraining F(j1)F(j2)conj(F(j1+j2)) against the edge atom) — exactly the unreachable region. On the honest box, CUE-vanishing triple constraints are weak (satisfied by CUE and small perturbations; the adversary re-optimizes positions to decohere in-box triangle correlations while keeping pair rows and the edge/double structure), so p0^(3) ~ p0^(2) is the likely honest outcome. Running M1 as specified would produce a gate decision about a data class no theorem in the program can deliver. Repair: re-scope rows to the attainable region (or to the region of the non-Hermitian repaired T1, if a consumption mechanism for non-Hermitian mixed traces is ever found — none is proposed), and inflate tau3 near the attainable boundary to reflect T1's error blowup (the proposal's own failure mode 3).

findings.claim: The Alternative-Hypothesis payoff (M6, and obstruction-evasion item 2) is empty: AH-structured laws do not violate connected-triple vanishing anywhere in the provable range, so the 'obstruction converted into a target' argument fails.
findings.argument: For half-integer-lattice (AH-structured) configurations, the triple observable A3(j1,j2) = Re[F(j1)F(j2)conj(F(j1+j2))]/N is large only when all three frequencies sit near dual-lattice resonances. The minimal non-degenerate triple resonances involve total support >= 2: e.g. (1/2, 1/2, -1) has |xi1|+|xi2|+|xi3| = 2, sitting exactly ON the closed-simplex boundary that every version of T1 excludes (T1 is an open-simplex sigma < 2 statement, and the proposal's own LP leaves edges free); full dual-lattice triples like (2,2,-4) are far outside. Inside the open total-support-<2 simplex — a fortiori inside the honest 2/3-box of finding 3 — AH laws SATISFY the triple-vanishing rows. This matches the known pattern (AH is precisely engineered to be consistent with all bandwidth-1 pair data; its deviations begin at the support boundary): the natural extension is that AH is consistent with all restricted-range n-level data, and the proposal provides no computation to the contrary. The claim that 'rigid arithmetic spacings generate triple resonances j1+j2=j3 in-band' is backwards: the resonances exist but are out of band. M6's 'potential first refutation of AH' — billed as 'the most significant pair-correlation-adjacent result since Montgomery' — should be expected to return the null result, and evasion item 2 loses its content.

findings.claim: Section 7.5(g) is overread as an 'existence proof that cubic accounting survives interactions': the cited RH-conditional result has Q EMPTY, so it demonstrates nothing about the interactions that actually kill Lemma C.
findings.argument: Under RH there are no off-line zeros: A = P, all mass is on-line, the matrix is PSD, and the Schur-Horn majorization argument of 7.5(g) (f(x) = -x^2/9 + x^3/18, N_d >= 0.85082) never faces a hyperbolic block, an X^{2y}-amplified eigenvalue, or a signed P-Q cross term. The interactions it 'survives' are on-line/on-line only — and even at degree 2 the campaign record shows the spectral (m-1)(m-2) level is destroyed by on-line interactions under RH+GUE, recovered only by the regrouping device, which is inherently quadratic (it relies on Frobenius positivity). The proposal half-admits this ('Lemma C is its unconditional extension with Q nonempty') but then uses 7.5(g) as evidence for exactly the step (off-line interaction control at odd degree) on which 7.5(g) is silent. Combined with finding 2, the honest statement is: there exists NO evidence, conditional or numerical, that cubic accounting survives Q-interactions, and there is a concrete counterexample class showing the proposed form does not.

findings.claim: Assorted mechanism slips: tr(G_aG_bG_c) is not real in general and must be symmetrized; the same-prime-power triple diagonal is O(1/l^3)-relative, not O(1/l); endpoint loglog/log losses at lambda_a -> 1 (admitted) interact badly with a gain the proposal itself estimates could be ~0.01.
findings.argument: (i) For non-commuting Hermitian A,B,C, conj(tr(ABC)) = tr(CBA) != tr(ABC); the certificate row must be Re tr(G_aG_bG_c) or the symmetrized sum over both cyclic orders — never stated, fixable, but it changes the LP observable (the proposal's A3 rows do take Re and Im, so the analytic side and the LP side are currently pricing different functionals). (ii) The exact-relation term n1n2 = n3 forces all three to be powers of one prime: Sum_p (log p)^3 Sum_{a,b} p^{-a-b} converges to O(1), contributing O(T) against the main term T*l^3, i.e. relative O(1/l^3); the stated O(1/l) is off by two logs (conservative direction, harmless, but indicates the error bookkeeping in the Mechanism was not carried through). (iii) The proposal's own failure-mode list concedes p0^(3) - 0.6725 might be ~0.01 while the lambda_a -> 1 endpoint erosion is loglog/log — at T-ranges where the parent certificate is barely positive, a 0.01 headline gain is inside the endpoint noise; no quantitative reconciliation is offered.

run2_killer.repairs: Three genuinely salvageable pieces, none of which is the thesis. (1) T1 as a standalone theorem: restate with the correct cross-window kernels. Two honest versions: (a) equal windows lambda < 2/3 (Hermitian, kernel supports (lambda,lambda,lambda), total < 2) — the corrected form of what the paper's 7.5(e) sketches, still the first unconditional order-3 correlation theorem for zeta (BGSTB is order 2), publishable; (b) the stronger repair: two-slot non-Hermitian compressions G_w = W(phi_w^L e_{tau_k}, phi_w^R e_{tau_l}); the slot windows pair cyclically, giving kernel supports s1 = min(lam_a^R, lam_b^L) etc., and setting lam_a^R = lam_b^L = s1 (cyclically) makes the prime-side budget Sum_w (lam^L + lam^R)/2 = s1+s2+s3 < 2 — the FULL Rudnick-Sarnak simplex, including one direction at bandwidth 1-eps, becomes reachable unconditionally. This repaired M2 is the real prize of the direction and survives all findings — but it feeds no known certificate (non-Hermitian products have no inertia/Schur-Jensen machinery). (2) M1 re-scoped: run the triple-row LP on the attainable region only (box j1,j2,j1+j2 <= (2/3)N for the Hermitian class), with edge-inflated tolerances; also run the AH-structured configurations expecting the null result, and separately run the full-simplex LP purely as an upper bound on what ANY future consumption mechanism could buy. Publish either outcome as the order-3 extension of the PairCeiling meta-theorem. The pair-only dual at N=128 (candidate certificate for the 0.6725 -> 0.6818 gap) is independent of every finding here and worth extracting regardless. (3) If a certificate arm is ever revived, the missing ingredient identified by finding 2 is a prime-side-computable POSITIVE interaction currency; one concrete candidate the proposal misses: mixed quartic traces tr(G_aG_bG_bG_a) = ||G_bG_a||_F^2 >= 0, unconditionally evaluable when the slot budget is < 2 (e.g. lambda_a = 0.7, lambda_b = 0.29), giving a sign-definite fourth-order functional that upper-bounds cross-window interaction mass — even-degree positivity at total support < 2 is the only visible route around the odd-degree sign problem, and it should be priced by the LP before any analytic work. Do not attempt rank_trace_cubic in its stated form; any restatement must carry vector-geometry hypotheses (u-w coupling of realizable blocks) and a proof they instantiate at zeta, which is a new open problem adjacent to the visibility wall.
literature_flags: Hejhal 1994 (triple correlation) and Rudnick-Sarnak 1996 (n-level, total Fourier support < 2): the proposal self-flags their exact unconditional/complex-ordinate status; must be verified against the originals before M2 is claimed as 'first in print' — in particular whether RS's remarks already cover complex ordinates unconditionally in restricted range.

Diaconis-Shahshahani exactness range for MIXED moments E[Tr U^{j1} Tr U^{j2} conj(Tr U^{j1+j2})]: the proposal asserts exact vanishing for j1+j2 <= N_matrix; the sharp range for mixed moments is due to Diaconis-Evans (2001) and the precise condition (max of total positive vs negative powers <= N) must be checked before the LP's t3 = 0 rows are set.

BGSTB24 = arXiv:2306.04799 (2023 posting; unconditional pair form factor, complex ordinates): the claim that its de-conditionalization technique extends verbatim to triple sums with composite-frequency MV is plausible but unverified; the repo's MV/Spacing.lean 'spacing_four' and 'two_point' lemmas being 'sufficient for third/fourth-moment off-diagonal analyses' is a repo assertion, not a proof.

AH triple-correlation structure: my resonance analysis (AH lattice laws satisfy in-simplex triple vanishing; first violations at total support >= 2) is derived, not recalled, and should be checked against the framework of arXiv:2507.06823 (GLSS Part II) before finding 4 is treated as settled.

Paper section 7.5(e)/(g) exact wording: whether the paper's 'diagonal method' claim for tr G^k in the RS range already notes the pairwise-min kernel obstruction for mixed windows (which would make finding 1 an error the parent authors implicitly knew), and the exact hypotheses of the 0.85082 cubic-weight computation (window cos(8s/5), RH-conditional, Q empty).

Proposal's citation of the 256-law scope note ('k >= 3 data outside design, triple-row LP the most informative next computation') is accurate per map-hooks; its use is legitimate, but note the same source states the pair band in j-units, which fixes the honest triple-row region of finding 3.
